record.title: Federal securities or derivatives-market authority
kv: Federal securities laws and the Commodity Exchange Act, each within its statutory perimeter.
A legally classified securities-market or derivatives-market activity calls for the applicable SEC or CFTC registration, designation, supervision, or rule route.
U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (public body); Commodity Futures Trading Commission (public body)

U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; Commodity Futures Trading Commission; SEC or CFTC offices acting under delegated authority; Self-regulatory organizations only within their separate statutory rulemaking roles

Classify the instrument, contract, and activity. Identify the exact entity and applicable SEC, CFTC, or SRO route. Recover current registration, designation, order, exemption, rulebook, and effective-date evidence.
Neither tokenization nor a technical ledger decides securities/commodity classification or creates SEC/CFTC permission.

U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission: SEC's Trading and Markets division describes its securities-market regulatory role; Exchange Act section 19 provides a Commission process for SRO proposed rule changes.
Commodity Futures Trading Commission: The Commodity Exchange Act provides CFTC designation/registration routes for defined derivatives-market functions.
